name: Alabama

statute.readVia: ALISON GraphQL API (alison.legislature.state.al.us/graphql), official legislature data

windshield.strip: transparent item, not red or amber, on the uppermost six inches of the windshield; no material reducing light transmission otherwise

frontSide.note: min 32% light transmission, max 20% reflectance, measurement tolerance of at least 3%

backSide.note: same 32% rule as front side for passenger cars

windshield.strip: uppermost six inches, transparent, not red or amber

backSide.note: windows tinted before factory delivery or permitted by federal law are exempt (§ 32-5C-3(6)); ALEA: darker tint behind driver as allowed by the manufacturer under federal law; outside mirrors on each side required

rear.note: same as back side (factory/federal-law tint); ALEA requires outside mirrors on both sides when darker tint is installed

tint.measuredHow: film + glass combined ("material or glazing ... which reduce light transmission")

tolerance.cite: Ala. Code § 32-5C-2(a)(2) ("measurement tolerance of at least 3 percent")

tint.dualMirrors: ALEA page: outside rearview mirrors on each side required when darker tint is installed behind the driver on multipurpose/recreational vehicles
tint.certificateOrSticker: Label visible from outside the vehicle certifying compliance required on tinted windows (§ 32-5C-6); ALEA says it must be affixed by a tinting dealer

medicalExemption.text: ALEA may issue an exemption on application supported by a written statement from a physician licensed in Alabama, for a vehicle owned by the person or in which the person is a habitual passenger; conditions set by ALEA; for light-sensitive porphyria it covers all areas the physician prescribes; a numbered decal is placed on the windshield (§ 32-5C-4). Apply: ALEA Driver License Division, Medical Records Unit, P.O. Box 1471, Montgomery, AL 36102, 334-676-7396.

penalty.text: Misdemeanor: 1st conviction fine up to $100 and/or up to 10 days; 2nd within one year up to $200 and/or 30 days; 3rd within one year up to $500 and/or 3 months

tint.lastAmended: 2021 (Act 2021-451 amended § 32-5C-2 to exempt personal vehicles of active or retired law enforcement officers; numbers unchanged since Act 96-534)
quotes: § 32-5C-2(a)(1): "With material or glazing applied or affixed to the front windshield which reduces light transmission through the front windshield."

§ 32-5C-2(a)(2): "...which reduce light transmission through the rear windshield or side windows to less than 32 percent or increase light reflectance to more than 20 percent, with a measurement tolerance of at least 3 percent."
§ 32-5C-3(4): "Any transparent item which is not red or amber in color which is placed on the uppermost six inches of the windshield."
§ 32-5C-3(6): "Any other vehicle, the windows or windshields of which have been tinted or darkened before factory delivery or permitted by federal law or regulation."
§ 32-5C-7: "...for a first conviction thereof shall be punished by a fine of not more than one hundred dollars ($100), or by imprisonment for not more than 10 days..."
ALEA: "On the windows behind the driver, darker tinting is permitted as allowed by the manufacturer of the vehicle by Federal Law."

helmet.conditions: All operators and riders of motorcycles/motor-driven cycles; not applicable in an enclosed cab or to autocycle operators

handheldPhone.fineText: Class C misdemeanor: 1st conviction (24 months) up to $50, 2nd up to $100, 3rd+ up to $150; first § (c)(1) charge dismissed if driver produces a hands-free device or proof of purchase; no custodial arrest
handheldPhone.cite: Ala. Code § 32-5A-350.1 (Act 2023-478; old texting law § 32-5A-350 repealed)

studdedTires.note: metal studded or safety spike tires allowed only 'when required for safety because of snow, rain, or other conditions'; no calendar season in statute

radarDetector.note: No Alabama statute banning radar detectors found; commercial vehicles over 10,001 lb banned federally (49 CFR 392.71)

openQuestions: § 32-5A-350.1 requires the driver to be observed lane-crossing without signal, swerving or driving impaired while holding the device, so it is not a pure primary handheld ban; effective date of Act 2023-478 enforcement (reported as June 2024 with warning period) not confirmed on an official page
Underglow / aftermarket lighting: no specific Alabama statute found (32-5-241 lists permissible lamps only)
Lift / frame height: no Alabama statute found
Radar detector: absence of state ban not confirmed by an official page
